name: Sydney/Kingsford Smith

runway.v: three runways: 16R/34L, the main one, 3,962 m; 07/25, 2,530 m; 16L/34R, 2,438 m (lengths agree with the AIP chart of 3 Sep 2026, which shows each 45 m wide)
runway.quote: 16R/34L – Main north south runway (3,962m) ... 16L/34R – Parallel north south runway (2,438m) ... 07/25 – East west runway (2,530m)

curfew.v: a curfew from 11 pm to 6 am; only listed quieter aircraft, including approved business jets under 34,000 kg, may operate, taking off to the south and landing to the north over Botany Bay
curfew.quote: A curfew period starts at 11 pm on a day and ends at 6 am on the next day.

slots.v: Level 3 airport: general and business aviation may not operate without a slot from ACL or Airservices. Requests go through the operator's authorised handling agent, or directly to ACL if the operator subscribes to OCS (the document's term). ACL works Monday to Friday 08:30 to 16:00 Sydney time, excluding public holidays; same-day and next-day requests after 16:00 go to Airservices (NOMC), as do requests on weekends and public holidays for Saturday, Sunday or Monday operations
slots.quote: No General Aviation / Business Aviation (GA / BA) operator is permitted to operate to or from Sydney Airport without first obtaining an Airport Slot from ACL or Airservices Australia (as relevant).

max_aircraft.v: the corporate aviation apron takes aircraft up to 22,000 kg MTOW and 32 m wingspan; larger aircraft must arrange parking with the airport before arrival
max_aircraft.quote: Access to corporate aviation apron restricted to 22,000KG MTOW/32M MAX wing span and BLW. ACFT in excess of this are to contact AD OPR prior to arrival for parking arrangements.

handling.v: ExecuJet runs the FBO and VIP lounge, open 24 hours
handling.quote: Execujet: FBO services and VIP Lounge H24. Civil and MIL ACFT. IS-BAH Stage II.

noise.v: noise abatement procedures and the curfew apply
noise.quote: Noise Abatement Procedures (NAP) and Curfew applies. Refer AIP DAP.

permits.v: aircraft must enter or leave Australia at a designated international airport unless permission was given first; non-scheduled international flights must also contact the Department of Infrastructure (DITRDCA) before the flight
permits.quote: All Aircraft must enter or depart Australia at an airport that is designated as an international airport

ppr.v: border notice only: non-scheduled flights must contact the local Australian Border Force and the Department of Agriculture no later than 72 hours before arrival or departure; NPPC approval is not required at Sydney (NPPC Airport Guide, July 2026)
ppr.quote: no later than 72 hours prior to the arrival or departure of the intended flight for non-NPPC applications.

notes: The ERSA entry is dated 9 Jul 2026, which was the newest edition found. The 3,962 m runway's designator could not be read reliably from the DAP chart text (ERSA lists 07/25, 16L/34R and 16R/34L, all 45 m wide), so the designator is left out. The ERSA states no distance from the city, no customs hours and no general opening hours. The curfew wording comes from Compilation No. 7 of the Curfew Act (16 Dec 2020); the latest compilation (C2024C00497, 14 Oct 2024) could not be read as text, so recheck section 6 against it. The 80-movement cap comes from the Demand Management Act compilation of 14 Jan 2011; the latest version was not checked. Under the DITRDCA page, the curfew shoulder hours are 11 pm to midnight and 5 am to 6 am, with limits on international passenger arrivals between 5 and 6 am. The curfew is legally enforceable, and dispensations are granted only in exceptional circumstances. Sydney observes daylight saving time (AEDT, UTC+11, in summer; ERSA header says UTC +10); the curfew is set in local time. Extra 'curfew_jets', 'curfew_direction' and 'movement_cap' keys were added under facts. 1 Nov 2026: re-read ERSA FAC YSSY 09 Jul 2026 (still the newest found): it has no customs/immigration line, no aerodrome hours (only 'ARO OPS (24HR)') and no PPR; the only prior approval is for Class 1 explosives. Added a country-wide permits rule from the Australian Border Force 'Aircraft requirements' page (updated 20 Oct 2026). Customs hours, IATA and PPR still not found on an official page; sydneyairport.com.au had no business-aviation page in search results. | 3 Nov 2026: the ABF page (updated 20 Oct 2026) and NPPC Airport Guide (July 2026; Sydney 'Not Required' for fewer than 10 and for 10 or more travellers) give the border notice, which is not an airport PPR, so 'ppr' stays on the missing list; neither gives customs hours. Sydney Airport's 'Operating at Sydney Airport' page says the airport is Level 3, 'No General Aviation / Business Aviation (GA / BA) operator is permitted to operate to or from Sydney Airport' without a slot from ACL Asia Pacific, requests go to ACL weekdays 0830 to 1600 local and otherwise to Airservices (NOMC); it publishes a separate GA/BA Conditions of Use and COU v5.5, both refused, so please download: https://assets.ctfassets.net/v228i5y5k0x4/17XJJkjWqSfGmH3sSL6Y9O/8d02342fb6e4cccb0d8f801e10535adf/General_and_Business_Aviation_-_COU.pdf and https://assets.ctfassets.net/v228i5y5k0x4/6Ufzb4atyU2D8i3TzB8iNy/07a18aac0508a418a5a0f9c568048d83/SYD_COU_v5.5.pdf. The aircraftnoise.sydneyairport.com.au operational-restrictions page was refused (robots). 5 Nov 2026: read the GA/BA Conditions of Use Version 1.0 (May 2026), so the slots rule moves to that newer source; it says nothing on parking, size limits, customs, curfew or fuel. Runway designators and IATA come from the operator's Aviation enthusiasts page (undated). Ground movement chart SSYAG01-188 (3 Sep 2026) prints the same three lengths: https://www.airservicesaustralia.com/aip/current/dap/SSYAG01-188_03SEP2026.pdf. Terminal hours (T1 02:30 to 23:00; customs for departing passengers from 04:00) are not aerodrome or GA customs hours and are not recorded. COU v5.5 was refused again. No FAC YSSY newer than 9 Jul 2026 surfaced, though other aerodromes have 3 Sep 2026 pages, so a newer one may exist. | 8 Nov 2026: nothing new; search still shows FAC YSSY 9 Jul 2026 as the newest ERSA entry; no official page found for customs hours or distance from the city. COU v5.5 not retried (refused twice). | 11 Nov 2026: Airservices' amendment calendar says the current ERSA is 3 Sep 2026 and the next is 26 Nov 2026; search still shows FAC YSSY 9 Jul 2026 as the newest page (re-read: no customs line, no aerodrome hours, no PPR; 'ACFT carrying livestock require prior approval FM AD OPR. Minimum 24HR notice.'). Re-read 'Operating at Sydney Airport': slot rule unchanged; it adds that 'All general and business aviation flights must use IATA service type 'D'' and handling agents give PVT flight numbers. The Curfew Act's latest compilation is C2024C00497 (14 Oct 2024); its contents page lists s6 'Curfew periods', s15 jet aircraft under 34,000 kg specified by the Minister, s18 and s20 dispensations, matching the rule on file; the full text PDF was not opened (permission not answered): https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A04984/2024-10-14/2024-10-14/text/original/pdf. Not opened (permission not answered): COU v5.5 (third try) and the ABF aircraft requirements page. Terminal hours page gives T1 02:30-23:00 only (passenger terminal, not recorded).
